reason: A rearranges sensibly for portrait: a large can, a strong headline and a clear CTA. However, 'fizz' wraps onto its own line as an orphan, the gap between the subhead and CTA is tight, and the peach circle has shrunk to a small blob in the corner. B leaves the wordmark tiny and floating in the middle of the green circle with dead space above it. Its headline, subhead and CTA are packed into a small band with a tiny subhead, and the bottom third is just a large empty peach circle, so it is lopsided and lacks hierarchy.

A looks like a shrunk copy of the original. The product, headline and CTA are small, there's a large dead band between the CTA and the tiny legal line, the GLACIER logo is pushed down into the teal circle, and the legal text floats mid-canvas over the blue circle. B scales the product, headline and CTA up to fill the portrait format with a clear top-to-bottom order and readable legal text. Its only flaws are minor: the headline nearly touches the side margins, and the gap between the logo and the product is a bit tight.

A is mostly the original shrunk and stacked into the space. The 'Garden-fresh fizz' headline and the oversized CTA pill run into both decorative circles. The can is shrunk to an icon whose label can't be read. The legal line wraps so 'details.' sits alone on a line, packed against the bottom edge over the circle. B actually rearranges the layout: the logo sits inside the left circle, the can inside the right one, the headline is a clear focal band and the CTA and legal text share a bottom row. Its flaws: the can is still tiny and its label unreadable, the legal text beside the CTA is cramped and competes with it, and the left edges don't quite line up.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark is pushed to the far left, halfway down, and sits on top of the green circle. The two circles are stacked and cramped in the left corner. The headline breaks so that 'fizz' sits alone on its own line. The body copy is jammed beside the CTA, and the bottle and button crowd the bottom and right edges. B: the reading order is clear (logo, headline, copy, CTA) and the bottle is grouped sensibly with the text. However, the end of the headline runs into the green circle, the CTA is oversized and nearly touches the body copy, there is dead space to the left of the bottle, and the text column is squeezed vertically.

A: The headline is dominant and reads clearly from logo to headline to subcopy to CTA, but the bottle is jammed against the left and bottom edges. It also sits on the yellow circle, and the CTA overlaps the green circle a little. B: The SOLSTICE logo is pushed off to the far left, away from the headline. 'fizz' crowds into the green circle, both circles are piled up in the top-right corner, and the CTA runs almost to the right edge. The subcopy wraps into a cramped three-line block beside the CTA, so B is fragmented and cramped.

B is the better resize. A's 'Find a Store' button has been blown up almost to the full canvas width, so it outweighs the headline. The button also sits right on the olive circle, which is an unwanted collision, and the bag is shrunk to a small, timid size. B keeps the original proportions: the bag is larger, the headline is bold, and the button is properly sized. Both orphan 'fizz' on a second line, and B still has flaws to fix: the logo-to-bag gap is tight and the bottom ~110px is empty apart from the olive circle.

A: the eyebrow is pushed out under the dark logo panel into the bottom-left corner, apart from the headline. The four-line headline fills the full banner height, edge to edge. 'Ships late June' breaks into a narrow three-word stack, and the legal text is as prominent as the body copy next to a tiny CTA. B is better ordered, with the eyebrow above a three-line headline and the CTA on the right, but it is still overcrowded: the logo is a nearly invisible speck in its panel, the body copy is jammed against the top edge, the legal block is cramped under it, and 'Ships late June' is set bigger than the CTA.

A drops the SOLSTICE logo entirely. Only an empty sliver of the dark header band is left at the top, so the brand is lost. The body copy is jammed right under the headline, 'Ships late June' is set almost as big as the CTA so the two compete, and everything is cramped. B keeps the logo band and the headline reads well, but the 'Reserve a Case' button is shrunk until it is illegible and pushed into a corner. 'Ships late June' and the legal text are also microscopic, while the oversized body copy runs against the left edge and pulls focus from the headline, so the CTA is buried and the hierarchy breaks. Both are broken. I pick A as slightly less bad because its CTA is still readable and prominent, but this is close to a guess.

A keeps a full-width header and a clean centred column, but the orange divider has moved from under the headline to below the body copy, there's a large empty gap between the headline and the body, and 'Ships late June' sits too far below the CTA. B's dark header bar doesn't reach the right edge (and leaves a sliver on the left), which breaks the brand frame. B also has a big dead gap between the eyebrow and the headline, leaves 'Ships late June' stranded far from the button, and shrinks the legal text to illegible.

A keeps the original's centered structure, but the headline sits jammed right under the header band and the space between headline, body copy and CTA is cramped. The orange divider has slipped onto the body copy and shows as an underline under 'released in', which is a collision, and the logo is shrunk very small. B is clearly broken: the dark header band covers only the left half of the canvas, the whole right half is empty apart from a stray floating divider line, and the tiny legal text is stranded in the bottom-right corner, so the layout is badly lopsided.

A: the orange divider has slipped down and now underlines 'Ships late June', so it collides with that text. The body copy is jammed straight under the headline with no breathing room, the CTA stretches almost edge to edge, and the bottom third is dead navy space. B: the white logo band stops short of the right edge, leaving a navy notch that looks broken. The divider is half-hidden behind the top of the CTA button, the body copy is small and crammed under the headline, and the bottom is also empty. B's broken band is the more visible brand defect, so A wins narrowly.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark is shrunk to a tiny size and pushed down to y≈150, where it floats inside the sage circle and leaves dead space above it. The subtitle and CTA are jammed together and the text is small for a tall format. B: the logo sits at the top at a good size, and the can, headline, copy and CTA are scaled up and stacked in a clear top-to-bottom order. Its flaws are the orphaned 'fizz' on its own line, a slightly tight gap between subtitle and CTA, and a shrunken peach circle in the bottom corner.

A rebuilds the stack for the 4:5 canvas. The logo sits at the top, the can is enlarged and the headline is big and dominant. Its flaws are that the headline nearly runs the full width with thin side margins, and the headline, CTA and legal line are packed tightly at the bottom below a loose gap under the can. B looks like a shrunk copy: the logo drops to y≈128 onto the teal circle and leaves dead space above it. The can and CTA are undersized, and the legal text is tiny and floats mid-lower with about 100px of empty space beneath it, so the canvas looks unbalanced and the content is bunched in the middle.

A rearranges the design into an organised banner: the logo sits in the blue circle, the can in the teal circle, then a large headline, with the CTA and legal text paired in a bottom row. But the can is shrunk until its SOLSTICE label can't be read, the sun detail is lost, and the 3-line legal text next to the CTA is tiny. B is just the original stack shrunk down. The can is tiny and its label unreadable. The headline, CTA and legal text are jammed together with no breathing room, and both circles show through behind the headline and CTA. The legal text wraps to leave the single word 'details.' on its own line, pressed against the bottom edge.

A reads clearly from logo to headline, subcopy and CTA, with the bottle beside them. Its flaws: the 'fizz' of the headline touches the green circle, the CTA pill is too big and heavy and sits close to the bottom edge, the headline-to-subcopy gap is tight, and the whole group crowds the centre while the far left is empty. B is clearly broken: the SOLSTICE logo sits on top of the green circle, the headline breaks to leave 'fizz' alone on its own line and nearly touches the top edge, the subcopy and CTA are squeezed side by side at the bottom with the CTA almost against the right edge, and the reading order is muddled.

A is cramped. The bottle runs almost from the top edge to the bottom edge. The 'fizz' of the headline crowds into a muddy stack of two overlapping circles in the top-right corner. The body copy is squeezed into a ragged three-line centred block, and the oversized CTA crowds the right edge, so the hierarchy feels jammed. B has a clearer order (logo, headline, one-line subhead, CTA on the right) and fits the banner better, but the bottle is cropped at the bottom edge and pushed into the left corner over the yellow circle, and the CTA is small and floats with an uneven gap.

A keeps the headline as the main element and the CTA at a sensible size. However, the headline wraps and leaves 'fizz' alone on its own line, the CITRINE logo sits tight against the top edge, and the stack sits high with only the olive circle filling the bottom. B centres the stack better, but its CTA pill is blown up to almost full width with thin side margins and becomes a white block that competes with the smaller headline; it also has the same orphaned 'fizz' and leaves empty space at the top.

A: the SOLSTICE logo is a near-invisible speck in a dark side panel. 'Ships late June' wraps onto two lines and is almost as large as the tiny 'Reserve a Case' button, which buries the CTA. The legal text is crammed directly under the body copy. Even so, the reading order (eyebrow, headline, body, CTA) holds up. B: the eyebrow sits under the logo panel, cut off from its headline. The 4-line headline fills the full height and touches the top and bottom edges. 'Ships late June' is squeezed into a 3-word vertical stack between the body copy and the CTA, and the legal text is jammed under a tiny button. B is more cramped and more broken up than A.

A keeps the logo bar, but the hierarchy is broken. The 'Reserve a Case' button and 'Ships late June' have shrunk to an unreadable size, the body copy is now bigger than the CTA, the legal text is about as big as the CTA, the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone and the headline runs almost to the canvas edges. B has a proper CTA and keeps the eyebrow, but the brand bar is cropped so the SOLSTICE wordmark is lost, the orange divider runs through 'our seaside' in the body copy, 'Ships late June' is as large as the CTA, and the whole stack is cramped with no margins.

In A, the dark header bar doesn't reach the canvas edges: there is a gap on the left and a wider one on the right, so it looks broken. A also leaves a large dead gap between the eyebrow and the headline, and 'Ships late June' drifts about 90px below the CTA it belongs to. B keeps the full-width header and a clean centred stack, but it moves the orange divider from under the headline to between the body copy and the button. B's 'Ships late June' still sits loosely below the CTA, and its eyebrow and legal text are very small.

A squeezes everything into the left half: the dark header bar stops at about x=380, the orange divider sits by itself in the empty right half, and the legal line is pushed to the bottom right. The result is a lopsided layout with a large dead zone. B keeps the original's centred structure and full-width header, but the divider now runs through the body copy, underlining 'released in'. Spacing between the headline, body and CTA is cramped, and the dark header bar takes up too much height.

A: the white logo header is cropped short and leaves a navy strip on the right, so the brand bar looks broken. The orange divider crashes into the top of the CTA, the body copy is jammed directly under the headline, and about 100px of dead navy space sits at the bottom. B: the header spans the full width and the text is larger and easier to read, but the orange divider now runs under 'Ships late June' like a stray underline (a collision). The body copy and CTA are crammed against the headline, the button nearly touches the side edges, and the bottom is still empty, but B's flaws are less damaging to the brand than A's broken header.

A breaks the reading order: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline, and the headline is crammed against the green circle at the top. There is also a large dead gap between the body copy and the can, though the CTA is well sized. B keeps the original order (brand, can, headline, copy, CTA), but its spacing is uneven, with big voids around the headline. Its CTA is stretched almost full width, its label text is tiny, and it is jammed near the bottom edge on top of the yellow circle.

A leaves about 110px of empty space at the top while the subhead and CTA are jammed together near the bottom, with almost no gap between them. Its subhead is small, and the CTA sits on top of the peach circle. B has better hierarchy and spacing: a larger, more readable subhead and CTA with even gaps. However, B's headline wraps with an orphaned 'fizz', and it moves the peach circle to the top-left, where it crowds the SOLSTICE logo and makes the top heavy, which changes the original's corner balance.

A turns the two background circles into a stacked pair of blobs in the left gutter that look like stray dots, not the original's corner accents. The CITRINE wordmark floats on its own to the left of the bag, and the CTA sits cramped against the bottom edge. B reads cleanly left to right (product, then brand and headline, then CTA) and keeps the circles as layered corner accents. Its flaws: the bag is jammed against the left and bottom edges, and the CTA pill awkwardly half-overlaps the green circle.

A: the CITRINE logo has shrunk to tiny text and sits low, inside the green circle, with dead space above it. The CTA button is jammed right under the headline with almost no gap, and the content block feels squeezed between empty space at the top and bottom. B: the logo is a proper size at the top, the pack is large and the headline and CTA have even, comfortable gaps. Its flaws are the headline breaking onto two lines with 'fizz' left alone on the second line, and a fairly empty bottom quarter where only the olive circle sits.

In A, the white logo header stops about two-thirds of the way across, leaving a navy gap on the right that looks like a rendering error. The orange divider floats alone in the right column above the CTA, and the body copy is shifted right of the headline's axis and jammed under it. B keeps a clean full-width header, but the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow sits right of the headline's centre axis. The headline also nearly touches the left canvas edge, the body copy is crammed near the bottom, the divider is gone, and the small CTA floats in a mostly empty right column. B wins narrowly; neither is ship-ready.

A: the dark logo block floats in the top-left with an arbitrary inset, and the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow sits under it, cut off from the headline, which breaks reading order. The three-line headline is jammed against the body copy column, and the legal text crowds the bottom edge. Still, the logo and hierarchy hold up. B: the orange divider runs straight through 'Yet' like a strikethrough, and the headline nearly touches the right edge. The SOLSTICE logo shrinks to an illegible speck in a large empty dark panel, which wastes a third of the banner and weakens the brand.

A keeps the original order (logo, can, headline, copy, CTA), but the SOLSTICE wordmark runs into the green circle, the gaps between can, headline and body copy are uneven and wide, the body copy is small, and the CTA nearly touches the side edges. B breaks the hierarchy: the headline sits above the brand wordmark and over the green circle, the logo is stuck between headline and copy, and the can is pushed below the copy, so the order is jumbled and the stack looks arbitrary, even though its CTA is better proportioned.

A: the content is crammed into the top two-thirds and leaves an empty band at the bottom. The headline breaks with a lone orphan word, 'fizz', and the subhead sits jammed against the CTA. The peach circle was moved to the top-left, where it crowds the logo and weakens the original's diagonal balance. B: keeps the original layout (green circle top-right, peach bottom-left) and the headline stays on one line, so the stack spreads more evenly down the canvas. However, the subhead has shrunk to near-fine-print size, the CTA is cramped tight under the subhead and is smaller, and the space above the logo is a little empty.

A reads cleanly left to right (bag → CITRINE/headline → CTA) and keeps the right hierarchy, but the bag is jammed against the top, bottom and left edges, the olive circle peeks out awkwardly behind the bag, and the CTA crowds the green circle. In B the two circles are stacked in a column on the left like stray dots, wasting the left third. CITRINE floats on its own far from the headline, the headline is pushed almost to the right edge, and the bag's label text is too small to read, so the layout looks scattered.

A keeps the original's top-to-bottom order, with a strong logo, bag, headline and CTA, but the headline wraps to leave 'fizz' as an orphan on its own line, the CTA sits close under it, and the bottom ~140px is empty apart from the olive circle. B wastes the top ~150px, shrinks CITRINE until it is tiny, jams the CTA about 10px under the headline, and lets the button overlap the olive circle, so the stack looks pushed down and cramped.

A keeps the full-width white logo header and gives the CTA its own clear right-hand column, but it has flaws: the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow is pushed right of the headline's centre, the headline almost touches the left edge, the orange divider is gone, and the body copy is jammed under the headline and sits close to the bottom edge. B's white header block stops at about two-thirds of the width, leaving a navy strip above and beside it that looks like a rendering bug. The divider sits stranded above the CTA, and the body copy is shifted off the headline's centre line and crowded under it.

A: the orange divider line runs straight through 'Blend Yet', so it reads like a strikethrough. The logo has shrunk to an illegible dot and wordmark inside a large empty dark panel, while the text column on the right is jammed top to bottom with no breathing room. B: the logo keeps its proportions, there are no collisions and the layout reads left to right. Its flaws: the eyebrow is pushed under the logo panel with a stray divider above it, the 3-line headline runs almost to the top and bottom edges, the right column of body copy, CTA and legal is cramped, and the legal text is too small to read.

A: the 'Find a Store' pill is oversized, spans almost the full width and outweighs the headline. The headline wraps badly, leaving 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and the cramped right-hand text column sits against a small can. B has a clear hierarchy, with a strong full-width headline and the can framed in the green circle, but its bottom row is cramped near the edge. The body copy there is tiny and sits on the peach circle, the CTA is small, and the SOLSTICE wordmark floats on its own at the left with no clear relationship to anything.

A uses a sensible left-to-right banner layout: can on the left, then logo, headline, CTA and legal stacked on the right. Its flaws: the CTA pill is oversized and nearly as heavy as the headline, the right circle crowds the headline and button, there's a dead gap between the can and the text, and the can label renders as 'SCLSTICE'. In B the headline is so big it wraps and leaves 'fizz' alone on its own line. The legal text is squeezed to an illegible size beside the CTA, the logo sits cramped on top of the circle above the can, and the can is jammed toward the bottom-left edge, so the hierarchy and spacing are broken.

A keeps the bottle as a real product element in a left column with text on the right, but the CTA pill is oversized and competes with the headline. The headline breaks with 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and the button sits cramped near the bottom edge. B shrinks the bottle to a tiny ornament in the top-right circle, which makes the key imagery trivial. Its body copy sits on the yellow circle and is jammed against the bottom-left edge, and 'fizz' is orphaned there too.

A: The orange divider rule runs through the body copy ('kitchen and released'), which is a real collision. The body copy is pushed off the headline's centre axis, the 'Ships late June' note sits awkwardly beside the button, and the huge dark left panel holds only a tiny logo, so it is mostly dead space. B: The dark header is cut off into a strange top-left block. The divider rule is stranded on its own at the far right, the body copy and legal line are tiny and hard to read, and the headline, body and CTA are scattered with no shared grid, leaving the right side empty. A still reads as a split banner and is the less broken of the two.

I scored both candidates 2 out of 5. B is the less bad of the two because it keeps the original's centred structure and a large orange CTA, but it has real faults. In A, the dark header has become a huge empty square that takes up the left half of the canvas, and the logo is shrunk to a speck in its corner. A's orange divider floats with no clear purpose, and the 'Reserve a Case' button is tiny and buried bottom-left next to 'Ships late June', so the hierarchy and the original feel are lost. In B, the orange divider strikes through the body copy ('our seaside'), which is a clear collision. B's logo is also shrunk to an illegible dot in the thin header bar. The headline, body, button and legal text are all jammed together with almost no breathing room.

A: the logo is shrunk to a tiny smudge in a wide, empty white panel. The two-line headline runs right up against the undersized 'Reserve a Case' button, and the body copy and 'Ships late June' are too small to read at banner size. B: the logo is a sensible size, and the logo/headline/body/CTA columns read cleanly left to right. However, the four-line headline fills almost the full height with no top or bottom margin, the body column and CTA are tiny, and the eyebrow has been moved away from the headline to sit under the logo.

A keeps the headline dominant across the full width, and logo, can and CTA read in a clear order. However, the bottom row is cramped: the small two-line subtitle sits on the peach circle and is squeezed against the CTA and the canvas edge, and the can is crowded inside the green circle. B is broken: the oversized CTA pill outweighs the headline. The headline wraps badly, leaving 'fizz' orphaned on its own line, and is pushed over the green circle. The can is shrunk and pushed off to the left, and the logo is off-centre and drifting, so the hierarchy and grid fall apart.

A: the headline is far too large and wraps, leaving 'fizz' alone on its own line and crowding out everything else. The legal text is tiny, squeezed in beside the CTA and wrapped so 'details.' sits alone, and the logo and can are jammed against the left edge on top of the circle. B: the logic is clearer, with the can on the left and the logo, a one-line headline, the CTA and readable legal text on the right. Its flaws: the logo, headline and CTA don't share an alignment axis (the logo is off-centre and the CTA is pushed right), the headline and logo sit over the corner circle, the can label looks distorted, and the left circle is cut off awkwardly.

A shrinks the bottle, the hero product, to a tiny thumbnail jammed into the top-right corner on the green circle, so the product almost disappears. Its body copy is small, sits on the yellow circle and hugs the bottom-left edge, and the headline leaves 'fizz' alone on its own line. B keeps the bottle at a usable size in a sensible left-product, right-copy banner layout. However, its CTA is oversized and heavy enough to compete with the headline, it crowds the bottom-right corner, the body copy sits on the green circle, and 'fizz' is also left alone on its own line.

Neither is shippable. A cuts the dark header down to a stub that covers only the top-left of the canvas, and the headline is jammed right under it. The orange divider is stranded alone at the far right edge, the body copy and legal line are tiny, and the right side is a loose, unbalanced column. B has a stronger banner structure: the dark brand panel with its logo sits on the left and the content on the right. But the orange divider runs through the body copy (over 'and released'), the body block is offset to the right instead of sharing the headline's axis, the logo looks small and lost in the big dark panel, and the legal line can't be read at this size. B is still the better of the two.

A keeps the original's centred stack and the CTA stays strong, but the orange divider cuts through the body copy ('our seaside'), the dark header is squashed into a thin strip with an unreadable speck of a logo, and the whole thing is cramped against the edges. B turns the dark header into a big empty square in the top-left that looks like a missing image, shrinks the logo to a tiny dot in that square's corner, leaves the divider floating on its own, and shrinks the CTA to a small pill at the bottom-left, so the hierarchy is badly weakened.

A reads left to right in clear zones: logo and eyebrow, then headline, body copy and CTA. Its flaws: the body copy is wrapped into a narrow 5-line column at near-illegible size, the CTA pill is tiny, the eyebrow sits under the logo far from the headline, and the overall look is dense. B shrinks the logo to a speck in an oversized white panel and runs the headline almost into the CTA pill, which is tiny and jammed into the top-right corner. Its 'Ships late June' text is as big as the button label and nearly touches 'Evenings', so the CTA is buried and the right side is cramped while the left is mostly empty.

A fits the portrait canvas with a larger can and headline and a body copy that wraps cleanly onto two lines. But the bottom is cramped: the CTA sits only about 25px under the body copy and about 38px from the bottom edge, while there is an 80px gap above the headline, so the vertical rhythm is uneven. B is just a shrunken copy of the square: the can is small, and the body copy is tiny and stretched almost edge to edge. The wordmark has dropped to about y=128, which leaves dead space at the top and roughly 140px empty at the bottom. The small CTA also weakens the hierarchy.

A reads left to right (logo, a can about 10 px tall, headline, CTA), but the headline wraps and leaves 'fizz' alone on the second line, the legal text squeezed under the CTA can't be read, and the product is too small to register. B puts the GLACIER logo under the headline, crops the can at the left edge, jams the legal line against the bottom edge under everything, and makes the CTA so big it outweighs the headline.

A uses a sensible two-column banner with a clear headline and CTA hierarchy, but the orange divider rule cuts straight through 'Botanical' like a strikethrough. The body column is also crowded against the right edge, and 'Ships late June' floats away from the button. B is a jumbled layout. The dark logo block is a lopsided slab in the top-left with an orphaned divider under it. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has fallen to the bottom-left, below the headline. The CTA is shrunk until it no longer stands out, and the legal text is squeezed into an illegible narrow column at the far right.

A is clean with no collisions and a strong headline and CTA. However, the orange divider was moved above the eyebrow, which breaks the original order. There is a large dead gap between the headline and the body copy, and the legal line is shrunk until it can't be read. B has a real collision: the orange divider runs right through 'Batch Blend' in the headline. Its logo and eyebrow are shrunk to tiny sizes, the gap under the headline is huge, and the body copy is crammed up against the CTA. B's legal text is more readable than A's, but that doesn't make up for these problems.

A is basically a shrunk copy of the original. The headline, CTA and especially the long single-line subtitle are undersized, there is about 140px of empty space below the CTA, and the content block sits high, so the canvas feels unbalanced. B uses the portrait shape better: the can and headline are bigger, the subtitle wraps neatly onto two lines, and the CTA has real weight. Its flaws are a cramped gap between the subtitle and the CTA (smaller than the other gaps) and a headline that runs close to the side edges.

A keeps the headline on one line and the CTA is strong. But the GLACIER logo sits under the headline, which reverses the brand-then-headline order. The can is a tiny fragment jammed against the left edge, and the legal line runs the full width, crammed against the bottom edge and up under the button. B has a more logical order (logo, then can, then headline, then CTA), but the headline breaks into 'Garden-fresh / fizz' with an orphaned word. Its can is a tiny afterthought under the logo, and the legal text is squeezed into a 4-line block of illegible micro type under the button. Both are cramped and none of the original's decorative circles survive.

A breaks the reading order. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow is stranded at the bottom left, far below the headline, and the divider floats under the logo block. The CTA is tiny and squeezed between the body copy and a column of illegible micro legal text, so the bottom row is a jumble of fragments. B keeps the header band and uses a sensible two-column banner with a strong CTA, but the orange divider cuts straight through 'Botanical' like a strikethrough, which is a clear collision. The headline also crowds the left edge, and the right column's top doesn't line up with the headline's top.

A: the orange divider runs straight through the second headline line ('Batch Blend'), which is a clear collision. The logo and eyebrow are shrunk very small, and there is a large dead gap between the headline and the body copy. B: nothing collides, and the eyebrow and body copy are at readable sizes. However, the divider has moved above the eyebrow, the blocks are spread out evenly with big gaps, so the CTA sits far from its copy and grouping is weak, and the legal text is shrunk until it can't be read.
